body: This seems indeed like a bug in the matcher.

IIRC, routes with same name are not supported at all so there may be no "proper" behavior here.
As Fabien said a little while ago, each route should be prefixed with the bundle alias to avoid duplicate route names.
But of course I may be wrong :)

@jalliot sure, but the goal to use it here is to overwrite a route defined in a shared bundle without having to avoid importing the file and copy-pasting all other routes. The behavior of the generator makes it possible so the matcher should be changed.
This is a known bug. Route names must be unique. Here, the uniqueness is not enforced because they are in different collection. It should be fixed and an exception should be thrown in this situation.

@fabpot Cool. So, what's the proper workflow then for overriding a route from a bundle? For example, suppose I import a resource from a third-party bundle, which contains about 5 routes. However, I want to override just one of them. Would the proper workflow be to not import the bundle's resource, copy in the 5 routes, and then customize the one route?

Thanks!
@weaverryan waiting this bug to be fixed, I don't see another way

After looking at the code, overriding an existing route is supported (implicitly by the `add()` method, but explicitly in the `get()` one). As the behavior cannot be changed at this point, I will work on a patch to solve the reported problem.

About my previous comment. The second example is not something that can do with YAML or XML, so it should never happen in real-life scenario. But if we want to support if (PHP is one of the configuration format), it complexifies the `RouteCollection` class a bit as we must save the parent of a collection to be able to remove the configured routes with a given name from all the parents.

For the first case, I agree that the pattern should be `/foo1` as we redefine the route with a new pattern. (however it would be `/foo` if `add` were called after adding `$collection`).
Regarding the second point, I don't really know what should be the result. It seems like a weird way to create the collections

Hi. I just upgraded my application to Symfony 2.0.4, and apparently this bug fix broke something else related to overwriting routes. I have a routing.yml file like this:

``` yml
admin_bundle:
    resource: "@DmAdminBundle/Resources/config/routing.yml"
    prefix: /admin

...
...

post_admin:
  pattern:   /admin/post/{id}/{action}.{_format}
  defaults:  { _controller: DmCommunityBundle:Post:admin, _format: html }
```

DmAdminBundle/Resources/config/routing.yml

``` yml
admin:
    resource: '@SonataAdminBundle/Resources/config/routing/sonata_admin.xml'

...
...

# overwrite dashboard pattern 
sonata_admin_dashboard: 
    pattern:  /
    defaults: { _controller: 'SonataAdminBundle:Core:dashboard' }
```

There are two problems here (in fact one problem with two different symptoms). In the first config.yml file:
- I create a new route, called post_admin, that has /admin/ prefix, just like the imported routing.yml file (not overwriting anything here). 
- Later one, I import SonataAdminBundle routing.yml file and overwrite the sonata_admin_dashboard route, in order to make the url /admin/ instead of /admin/dashboard. It used to work fine until 2.0.3, but now it doesn't work. An exception is thrown saying: 

```
Route "post_admin" does not exist. (problem #1)

or

Route "sonata_admin_dashboard (problem #2)
```

The route itself works, I mean, if you put the URL in the browser, it matches, but when you try to generate a url using {{ path }} or {{ url }}, it can't find the route. Interesting though is the fact that console router:debug display both routes:

```
php app/console router:debug

...
post_admin                                      ANY    /admin/post/{id}/{action}.{_format}
sonata_admin_dashboard                          ANY    /admin/
...
```

As I understood by the comments above, overwriting routers were not really meant to be available, but they are and I'm pretty sure I'm not the only one using it (and I believe this is very useful). Anyone can reproduce the problem above? I'm holding off upgrading because of this.

Thanks,

Carlos

issue.title: [Routing] Import prefix can conflict with route patterns
issue.body:
I believe this is a result 5c8a2fb48dfe09537db6ebdd77a52a3c90f409fe, which was a fix for #2139.

I have the following in my app's `routing.yml`:

``` yml
backend:
    resource:   @MyBundle/Resources/config/routing/backend.yml
    prefix:     /backend

backend_homepage:
  pattern: /backend
  defaults: { _controller: MyBundle:Backend:index }
```

This causes the `backend_homepage` route to be dropped after compilation, presumably because it conflicts with the import prefix. This would be understandable if the imported file had a route with `pattern: /`, but it does not (all routes have lengthy patterns).

If I reverse the order and define `backend_homepage` before the first import with `prefix: /backend`, everything is fine. Still, I consider this a work-around, as the prefix should logically not be responsible for dropping another route which really has no pattern conflict.
